data.name: Network_Intro
data.value: Choose the internet connection (WAN) and the adapter connected to the customers' Wi-Fi access point (LAN), then click "Share the internet".

data.name: Network_Problem_NotAdministrator
data.value: The service is not running with administrator rights. Run it as the Windows service or from a "Run as administrator" prompt.

data.name: Network_Problem_NotWindows
data.value: Connection sharing only works on Windows.

data.name: Network_Problem_NoLanAdapter
data.value: No second network adapter for the customer network. Plug in the adapter connected to the access point, or turn on Windows Mobile hotspot.

data.name: Network_Problem_AdapterNotFound
data.value: The chosen adapter no longer exists (unplugged or uninstalled).

data.name: Network_Problem_SameAdapter
data.value: The internet connection and the customer network must be two different adapters.

data.name: Network_Problem_WanNoGateway
data.value: The internet connection has no gateway: it does not seem to reach the internet.

data.name: Network_Problem_LanDown
data.value: The customer network adapter is disconnected (cable unplugged or access point off).

data.name: Network_Problem_IcsSubnetConflict
data.value: IP address conflict: the internet connection already uses 192.168.137.x, which Windows reserves for sharing. Change your router or modem's network.

data.name: Network_Problem_MobileHotspotOff
data.value: Windows Mobile hotspot is off. Turn it on in Settings > Network & internet > Mobile hotspot.

data.name: Network_Problem_IcsFailed
data.value: Windows refused to change connection sharing.

data.name: Network_Problem_IcsNotActive
data.value: The configured sharing is not active in Windows. Click "Share the internet" to turn it back on.

data.name: Network_Problem_GatewayIpConflict
data.value: IP address conflict: another device uses the gateway address. The access point is probably in router mode: switch it to access point / bridge mode.

data.name: Network_Problem_DevicesOutsideSubnet
data.value: Some devices have addresses outside the hotspot network. The access point may hand out its own addresses: turn off its DHCP / router mode.

data.value: Recent phones use a different "private / random" MAC address for each Wi-Fi network. That is normal: it stays the same on this network. To whitelist a device, always use the MAC shown here.

data.name: Terms_Default
data.value:
Wi-Fi access is reserved for customers with a valid code or account.
You agree to use the internet lawfully: no illegal activity, no downloading of protected works without permission, no harm to other users or to the network.
The time and data of your code are counted as explained at the counter. A code can only be used on the number of devices it allows.
For network security and to comply with the law, your device's address (MAC), its IP address and connection times are recorded.
The business may cut off access in case of abuse. The service is provided without any guarantee of speed or availability.
